summary: Nonce replay + cookie path normalization causing interactive SSO login loop in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: After upstream IdP update, a subset of FinSight users experience an interactive SSO loop when attempting to sign in to the Redwood Console on their private deployment. The browser repeatedly redirects to the IdP sign-in page and never lands back on the console. API keys and machine-to-machine auth are unaffected; only interactive web sessions are impacted.

Impact: ~12% of active console users (reported across two teams) cannot complete a login; they remain skirted out to the IdP and back repeatedly. This is preventing admin operations and delaying model rollouts.

Initial hypothesis: Identity proxy is setting a session cookie against an unexpected path due to URL normalization of encoded slashes in the IdP redirect_uri/relay_state. The IdP now returns a redirect with an encoded slash (%2F) in the relay path; some upstream ingress proxies normalize/decode that value when forwarding, causing the identity-proxy to see a different effective path vs. what the browser uses. The effect is two different Set-Cookie Path values across the handshake, which means the browser does not send the expected session cookie on the final console redirect, leading to repeated re-auth.

Notes: Customer reports this started after a routine IdP upgrade last Thursday. They are on the Private deployment (VPC) with our identity-proxy behind an internal nginx ingress that has allow_encoded_slashes off by default.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure private deployment with identity-proxy mounted at /sso/proxy/tenant-a
2) Configure IdP to include relay_state=apps%2Fconsole%2Ftenant-a (encoded slash in path segment)
3) From a new incognito browser, attempt console login and follow IdP redirect flow
4) Observe repeated redirects back to IdP and no persistent console session cookie being used on final redirect
logs: identity-proxy (2026-03-09T14:02:07Z) INFO Set-Cookie: rw_session=eyJhbGci...; Path=/sso/proxy/tenant-a; HttpOnly; Secure
browser request to /sso/proxy/tenant-a/apps/console/tenant-a did not include rw_session cookie (cookie path mismatch)
identity-proxy (2026-03-09T14:02:08Z) WARN session not found for relay_state -> redirecting to IdP
investigation_notes: Support reproduced locally with a minimal nginx ingress that had 'merge_slashes on' and 'allow_encoded_slashes off' — ingress decoded %2F into / before proxying to identity-proxy.

When ingress decoded the path, identity-proxy set Set-Cookie Path=/sso/proxy/tenant-a but browser final redirect used /sso/proxy/tenant-a/apps/console/tenant-a, which meant cookie did not match the requested path.

Captured curl traces and browser devtools show two Set-Cookie headers during SAML handshake in some flows (IdP-issued cookie via IdP domain + identity-proxy cookie). The important mismatch is the Path attribute differing because of decoding behavior upstream.

Hypothesis validated by toggling ingress to 'proxy_preserve_host on' and 'allow_encoded_slashes on' — with allow_encoded_slashes enabled, the path was not decoded and session cookie Path aligned with browser path, resolving the loop.
Customer's ingress had recently been upgraded by their infra team; change logs show a default change that disabled allow_encoded_slashes in the new image, explaining the regression timing.
customer_communication: 2026-03-09 15:10 - Aisha Patel: Acknowledged case, asked customer for SAMLRequest/Response dumps and their ingress config.
2026-03-09 18:02 - Customer (FinSight): Uploaded SAMLResponse and nginx ingress config; confirmed they rolled a new ingress image last Thursday.
2026-03-10 09:24 - Support (Lena Thompson): Confirmed reproduction and provided temporary mitigation steps to FinSight (see workaround).
2026-03-11 11:45 - Customer: Applied ingress config change in staging and observed successful logins; scheduling prod change window.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Support: Notified customer that an identity-proxy hardening patch will be released to make cookie Path assignment robust to decoded vs encoded relay_state.
workarounds: Short-term (customer): Update ingress/nginx config to enable 'allow_encoded_slashes on' and ensure proxy doesn't decode relay_state. Confirm login flow after change.
Alternative short-term: Configure identity-proxy to set session cookie Path=/ (root) as a temporary mitigation — reduces cookie scoping but resolves path mismatch.
If neither option available: IdP can be configured to avoid encoding slashes in relay_state (use a token or base64 blob instead of raw encoded path).
resolution_notes: Engineering assigned: identity-proxy team (Lena Thompson, Marco Ruiz)

Hotfix plan: Add defensive logic in identity-proxy to canonicalize relay_state consistently (treat %2F and / equivalently when deriving cookie Path) and a feature flag to force Path=/ for affected deployments.
PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/584 (adds canonicalization and feature flag), tests added to simulate decoded/encoded relay_state variants.
Staging: Patch deployed to staging 2026-03-11; FinSight confirmed staging login success.
Rollout: Target production rollout for 2026-03-13 in a canary-first deployment. Customer advised to apply ingress config workaround if they cannot wait for the patch.
next_steps: 1) Complete code review and merge PR #584 (identity-proxy) — assigned Marco Ruiz
2) Run additional canary cycles in us-east and monitor session creation/console-login 10-minute windows
3) Customer to schedule prod ingress image update OR accept our patch and we will coordinate canary rollout
4) Postmortem doc linking root cause to ingress default change and steps to avoid future regression. Add an entry to the SSO runbook.
